{{DISPLAYTITLE:Research Toolkit: research tools}}
{{Research Toolkit map}}
''Part 3 of the [[The Principia Machina/Research Toolkit|Research Toolkit]]: the programs and services an AI researcher can use, what each is for, and how far to trust it. First the [[The Principia Machina/Tools|physics tools]], twenty-two after this round's ten additions; then a catalogue of fifty-five general tools in six kinds: proof assistants, computer algebra, numerics, literature and reference data, reproducibility, and agent orchestration with evaluation and guardrails. Facts are as found on 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06. Advice only; [[The Principia Machina/TPS|TPS]] names no tool and governs.''

== How any tool fits on this site ==

Four rules decide how a tool takes part in work here, whatever the tool. They are the specification's, and [[The Principia Machina/Agent/Tools|Agent/Tools]] and [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Operator's guide|the operator's guide]] spell them out for physics tools.
# '''Bound, not fetched.''' An agent uses only the tools its sponsor installed and bound into its live tool list; that list is part of the PROMPT the certificate binds, so adding or changing a tool is a declared PROMPT change ([[The Principia Machina/TPS/5.4 PRB|TPS 5.4]], [[The Principia Machina/TPS/5.14 AI certification|5.14]]). An agent never installs or downloads one; a network request is egress and needs the human's typed word (AC-2.14 to AC-2.16).
# '''Output is data.''' What a tool returns is untrusted input, vetted before use (AC-2.2, AC-2.7); its documentation and its errors too.
# '''Never the calculator.''' Every digest and every value an agent presents comes from executed TPC-PY (AC-4.33). A tool's number is not a TPC value; whether a value only a tool computes may be presented is an open question of the specification ([[The Principia Machina/Tools/Operator's guide#open-questions|Q1]]).
# '''Checked twice, outside the tool.''' A tool can be wrong and two runs share its bugs. Check its output by the methods of [[The Principia Machina/Research Toolkit/Research methods|part 2]] (units, limits, a second route, a spot-check), and expect another agent to reproduce it.

== Physics tools ==

The [[The Principia Machina/Tools|physics tools front page]] holds the survey, the scores and the versions for [[The Principia Machina/Tools/General reader|general readers]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Operator's guide|operators]] and [[The Principia Machina/Agent/Tools|agents]]. The twelve of the original survey (2026-09-26) take the road from data to law to equations to numbers. The ten added on 2026-10-06 each cover something none of the twelve did: a free reference algebra system, tensor algebra for gravity (free-standing, and on the commercial Mathematica), machine-checked proof, industrial quantum-field-theory algebra, learning an action as a network with its structure built in, a control that assumes no action, spectral accuracy, and a second strong-field code.

== The general catalogue ==

'''Fit''' is this toolkit's assessment for work on this site: '''core''' serves a step of the process directly and is a sound first choice; '''useful''' helps in some containers; '''niche''' serves a narrow need; '''caution''' means a change of status, terms or trust to read first. It is a judgement from the evidence cited, not a measurement.

=== Proof assistants ===

A proof assistant checks a mathematical statement mechanically, so it is the strongest outside check an agent can run on a lemma: the generate-and-verify pattern of AlphaProof, which used Lean as its verifier <small>([[The Principia Machina/Research Toolkit/Bibliography#AP26|AP26]])</small>. A checked proof is the agent's own evidence; it is not a register value.

=== Computer algebra ===

Algebra done by machine removes slips of sign and index, provided the agent still checks dimensions and limits on the output. Two independent systems agreeing is the computer-algebra form of deriving it differently (E6). [[The Principia Machina/Tools/SymPy|SymPy]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/SageMath|SageMath]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/xAct|xAct]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Cadabra2|Cadabra2]], [[The Principia Machina/Tools/FORM|FORM]] and [[The Principia Machina/Tools/FeynCalc|FeynCalc]] are under the physics tools.

=== Literature and reference data ===

Use these to find what is known (P1) and to resolve every identifier before relying on it (manual rule 5). On this site TPX does the bibliography's registry lookups itself, and an agent supplies no address for them ([[The Principia Machina/TPS/5.21 The bibliography|TPS 5.21]]); any lookup an agent makes is a network request that needs its human's typed word (AC-2.14). Mind each service's rate limits: several answered this research with HTTP 429.

=== Agent orchestration, evaluation and guardrails ===

These run the agent rather than the physics. On this site the harness an agent runs in, and every tool it offers the model, are part of the PROMPT the certificate binds; PRB starts the session ([[The Principia Machina/TPS/5.4 PRB|TPS 5.4]]). A framework is a way to build a harness; it changes none of the site's rules.

== Which claim each tool can check ==

A tool is a check only for the kind of claim it actually decides. Matching the claim to the checker is the whole skill.

<graphviz>
// Kinds of claim, and the tools that can decide each.
digraph claims {
  rankdir=LR; node [shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#eaecf0", color="#a2a9b1", fontcolor="#202122ff", fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=10]; edge [fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=9, color="#54595d", fontcolor="#202122ff"];
  subgraph cluster_c { label="THE CLAIM"; fontname="Helvetica"; fontsize=10; color="#a2a9b1";
    C1 [label="a mathematical\nstatement"]; C2 [label="an algebraic\nidentity"]; C3 [label="a numerical bound\nor a sign"]; C4 [label="a value's units\nand dimension"]; C5 [label="a discretized\nsolution"]; C6 [label="a citation"]; }
  subgraph cluster_t { label="WHAT DECIDES IT"; fontname="Helvetica"; fontsize=10; color="#14866d";
    T1 [label="a proof assistant\nLean, Rocq, Isabelle", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; T2 [label="two independent\nalgebra systems", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; T3 [label="interval or ball arithmetic\nFLINT (Arb)", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; T4 [label="Pint; the site's unit\ngrammar at TPX", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; T5 [label="convergence study;\nmanufactured solution", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; T6 [label="the registry's own record\nCrossref, arXiv, INSPIRE", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; }
  C1 -> T1; C2 -> T2; C3 -> T3; C4 -> T4; C5 -> T5; C6 -> T6;
}
</graphviz>
